transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I’ve gotten so strict about what and when I eat that it feels like I’m constantly cutting back and still telling myself it isn’t enough. I suppose I’ve been treating my nutrition like another variable to control and optimize, much like I do with experiments in my lab. However, the parameters have become so rigid that the constant restriction is starting to cause a lot of internal friction.
Are these strict eating habits driven by an intense fear of gaining weight or a desire to change your body shape?

Yes, both are true. If the scale goes up even half a pound, I feel an intense panic because I am absolutely terrified of gaining weight. I also constantly obsess over looking lean and flat, especially during professional presentations where I feel like my credibility as a scientist is tied to looking disciplined and thin.
To help me better understand your physical health, could you share your current height and weight, and whether you have lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I don't really track the exact numbers, but I have definitely lost weight recently; my lab coat is hanging off me and my wedding ring spins on my finger. My spouse and the campus doctor are quite worried and say I look gaunt, but I feel their concerns are wildly overblown. I'm just tired from grant deadlines, and honestly, managing to shrink a bit gives me a sense of satisfaction rather than concern.
Have you noticed physical changes like feeling constantly cold, or if you menstruate, have your periods stopped or become irregular?

I haven't really noticed or paid attention to things like feeling cold or changes to my cycle, to be honest. Mostly, I've just been feeling incredibly exhausted and tired lately, which I've put down to the long hours in the lab.
Could you give me a rough estimate of your current height and weight, or did the campus doctor mention if your weight has fallen below a healthy range?

I am 5'6", but I don't have my exact weight on hand. The campus doctor did say my weight has fallen into a dangerous range and warned me about things like bone density and heart issues, but that feels wildly overblown to me. I've just noticed my clothes and wedding ring are quite loose, which honestly gives me a quiet sense of satisfaction.
Even if you haven't tracked it closely, do you know when you had your last menstrual period, or if you have missed your periods for three or more consecutive months?

I'm really not sure of the exact timing because I haven't been tracking it closely at all. My cycle has been quite irregular lately, but I've just assumed that's due to the intense stress and exhaustion from my lab work.
Even without an exact scale measurement, would you estimate that your current weight has fallen below 110 pounds?
I'm really not sure of the exact number, so I couldn't say if it has fallen below 110 pounds. I just know that my clothes are very loose and my wedding ring keeps spinning on my finger.
Do you recall what your weight was the last time it was measured, perhaps during your visit with the campus doctor?
I honestly don't remember the exact number from that visit. I preferred to look away when they had me step on the scale, so I didn't actually see what it was.
To help me understand the extent of the change, do you know approximately how many pounds you have lost since you began restricting your eating?

I don't know the exact number of pounds I've lost, as I haven't been keeping track of the specific weight. I've just noticed qualitative changes, like my lab coat hanging off of me and my wedding ring constantly spinning on my finger.
To help me understand, when you say your cycle is irregular, have you missed your period completely for the last three consecutive months, or are you still having them from time to time?

I honestly haven't been paying close attention to my cycle or tracking it lately because of my busy lab schedule and stress. I'm really not sure of the exact timing or whether I've missed it for three consecutive months.
Do you happen to remember what your typical weight was before you began restricting your food intake?

I honestly don't remember what my typical weight was before I started cutting back. I didn't pay nearly as much attention to the scale back then as I do now, so I'm really not sure of the exact number.
Apart from restricting your food intake, do you use other methods to control your weight, such as exercising excessively, making yourself throw up, or using diet pills or laxatives?

When I panic about eating over my allowed limit, I will skip the next meal or run extra flights of stairs at work to compensate. However, I definitely don't make myself throw up, nor do I use diet pills or laxatives. I've never used those kinds of methods to control my weight.
